loss/p: Softmax hands back probabilities: zero point seven, zero point two and zero point one.
loss/y: Say option zero turns out to be right, so y is zero. The loss is one number that says how bad the guess was, and it looks only at that option's probability.
loss/L: The loss, L, is minus the log of it. Minus the log of zero point seven is about zero point three six.
loss/wrong: Had option two been the right one, it would be minus the log of zero point one: two point three zero. Less probability on the truth, more loss.
curve/curve: Here is the loss, minus log p, for every p from zero to one. The arrow reads “goes to”: a p of zero point seven goes to a loss of zero point three six.
curve/one: At p equal to one, a confident right answer, the loss is zero. It never dips below zero, because the log of a probability is never positive.
curve/zero: As p falls toward zero, the loss climbs without limit, toward infinity, infinity. A confident wrong answer costs the most.
scores/s: Now start from scores: two, one and minus one, with option zero right. Softmax raises e to each score and adds them up: the total, T, is ten point four eight.
scores/py: The right option's probability, p of y, is e to its score, over the total: e squared, over ten point four eight.
scores/quot: The log of a quotient is the log of the top, minus the log of the bottom: ln of e squared, minus ln ten point four eight.
scores/undo: ln undoes e to a power, so ln of e squared is just two, the score itself. And ln ten point four eight is about two point three five.
scores/flip: The loss is minus that log, which flips the subtraction: two point three five minus two, or zero point three five.
scores/rule: Any scores go the same way. The loss is the log of the total, minus the right option's score, s of y.
uniform/init: When all the scores are equal, every option gets the same share. With C options, that share is one over C: ten options get a tenth each.
uniform/recip: So the loss is minus ln of a tenth. One over a number flips the sign of its log, so that is ln ten: about two point three zero.
uniform/logC: For any C, equal scores give a loss of ln C, whichever option is right.
uniform/eight: With eight options, write eight as two cubed, and the power comes out in front: ln eight is three ln two. That is three times zero point six nine three, about two point zero eight.
